The same instance can be reused: LoftPlayer.tsx:64-81 does not reset its state to loading or key the Player when fileId changes, and line 108 renders the same component type with the new url. loadYouTubeIframeApi.ts:69-74 clears the cached promise on a failed load, so B's later load can succeed.

unspecified_scores.reason: The IFrame API load has to fail for one video, succeed for another, and then the same player instance has to return to the first (for example A→B→A in a collection or through navigation). The user then sees an empty black player box with no link and no retry, until the page reloads.
Every question about a .loft video with a position now reads one small file from disk, even when the profile cannot see images, and the user notices nothing.
The url field would need surrounding whitespace, and the app does not write .loft files that way, so the file would have to be hand-edited before a fetch could get a padded URL.

specification_compliance: I6: the YouTubeEmbed sequence in F2 (a failed load, then a different video, then the failed id again on the same instance) renders an empty box rather than a link, which contradicts 'it never renders nothing'.
I4b: in the no-row refresh path, OSError/ValueError and an unusable url map to 404 (router.py:259-305). AmbiguousPath cannot occur there because resolution is non-strict.

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: When LoftPlayer's fileId changes, it keeps showing the previous content and passes the new fileId with the old url to the embed until the new fetch resolves.
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: Moving between .loft files, for example to the next video in a collection, briefly mounts or keeps the previous video's player under the new fileId, which can cause a short flash of the old video.

regression_risks: YouTubeEmbed's failedVideoIdRef guard interacts with instance reuse across fileId changes in LoftPlayer.
